teaser: Deciding what to buy and buying it are two businesses: custom explorer work and commodity town planner work. Give an open path and a better deal.
core_idea: A purchase has two moments, the decision (ending in a decision record: X, on Y, quantity Z) and the purchase. They are two businesses on a Wardley map: helping someone decide is custom, personal explorer and villager work, agnostic about where they buy; buying is a standard commodity for town planners. The strategy is no lock-in: map the do-it-yourself path from twenty-five steps to one, and sell a service that does it, for time, trust, execution, expertise and volume prices.

quotes.text: The key point is to separate the decision of what to buy from the operation of buying it.
your service has to be the better deal, not the only way
quotes.why: The open path, and a better deal.

quotes.text: It gets very unique, very fast.

figures.caption: A Wardley map of a purchase: the decision on the custom side, the purchase on the commodity side, the record between.
The two moments: deciding, which ends in a decision record, and buying, done by the person or by a service.
